theme: Glutathione-centred redox defence and detoxification of reactive metabolites
story: The centre is glutathione: its synthesis and recycling (GCLC, GSS, OPLAH, GGT1 and their inherited deficiencies), its catabolism and transmembrane transport, and the cystine and glutamate supply that feeds it. Around this core sit the jobs glutathione does, namely ROS detoxification, cell redox homeostasis, methylglyoxal and aldehyde detoxification, protein repair and suppression of ferroptosis, while NADPH regeneration and isocitrate metabolism (including the IDH-linked 2-hydroxyglutarate defect) supply the reducing power that keeps glutathione reduced. As a whole the cluster describes the cell's thiol-based antioxidant and electrophile-detoxification system; ACY1 deficiency and nonribosomal peptide synthesis are peripheral passengers tied in through amino-acid/peptide chemistry.

theme: Nephric duct and ureteric bud formation in early kidney
story: The core is the earliest stage of kidney development: intermediate mesoderm gives rise to the nephric (mesonephric) duct, which then buds to form the ureteric bud, which elongates and branches. Pronephros and mesonephros development represent the transient precursor kidneys along this axis, while organ induction, epithelial tube formation and regulation of ureteric branching describe the inductive and morphogenetic mechanics, and ureter morphogenesis is the eventual outcome. Together the cluster traces the duct lineage of the urogenital system from mesoderm to ureter.

theme: Non-vesicular lipid transfer and phospholipid flipping between membranes
story: The centre is movement of lipids between and across membranes: phospholipid, glycolipid, glycosphingolipid and ceramide-1-phosphate transfer proteins, PI/PC exchange between ER and Golgi, and P4-ATPase/TMEM30A flippases that translocate aminophospholipids to the cytosolic leaflet. Synthesis of PI supplies a key cargo lipid, and the two module descriptions add the flippase machinery and its membrane-trafficking context (COPII export, endocytic uncoating). The cluster as a whole is about how cells set and maintain the lipid composition and asymmetry of their organelle and plasma membranes.

theme: TCR proximal signalling driving T cell activation and differentiation
story: The core is T cell receptor signalling at the immunological synapse: phosphorylation of CD3 and TCR zeta ITAMs, ZAP-70 recruitment, and downstream ITK/PKC signalling. The blood transcriptional modules for T cell activation and T cell enrichment, plus the IL2/IL7/TCR network, read out this activation state, while the CD8 alpha-beta and gamma-delta differentiation terms describe the developmental consequences. Together the cluster depicts antigen-receptor-triggered T cell activation and its fate outcomes.

theme: Hormonal and nuclear receptor control of lipid/glucose metabolism
story: The centre is the switch between fed and fasted lipid metabolism: glucagon-PKA signalling phosphorylates key metabolic enzymes, AMPK inhibits ChREBP, and PDE3B (insulin's antagonist of cAMP) closes the loop. The LXR (NR1H2/NR1H3) transcriptional programmes for lipogenesis, gluconeogenesis and adipose lipolysis provide the transcriptional arm, and triglyceride catabolism, triglyceride synthesis restraint, fatty acid homeostasis, VLDL remodelling and adipose development are the metabolic outputs. As a whole the cluster describes how hormones and nutrient sensors coordinate triglyceride storage versus mobilisation.

theme: Thymic T cell selection, survival and tolerance
story: The centre is thymocyte development: positive and negative selection, control of immature T cell proliferation, and the balance of thymocyte apoptosis that eliminates self-reactive cells. Calcineurin signalling, Fas-pathway restraint and activation-induced cell death describe the survival/death signalling that underlies selection, while Treg development (RUNX1/FOXP3), CD8 and gamma-delta differentiation, and thymocyte migration describe the lineage outcomes. Together the cluster is about how the thymus produces a self-tolerant T cell repertoire.

theme: DNA damage-induced G2 checkpoint and p53 regulation
story: The core is the G2 DNA damage checkpoint: damage from gamma radiation triggers checkpoint signalling that degrades phosphorylated Cdc25A to block mitotic entry, with GTSE1 and MASTL governing recovery and mitotic progression afterward. In parallel, p53 is stabilised and activated through phosphorylation and control of its degradation (including COP1 autodegradation), and induces DNA repair genes. As a whole the cluster describes how cells halt the cycle after DNA damage, engage p53 and later resume mitosis.

theme: Craniofacial and limb skeletal morphogenesis
story: The cluster centres on building the embryonic skeleton: cartilage morphogenesis, osteoblast development and direct (intramembranous) ossification provide the tissue-level processes. These are deployed in specific structures, namely the face, nose, viscerocranium and cranial sutures, and the fore- and hindlimbs and digits. Together the terms describe skeletal patterning of head and limbs, regions that share developmental regulators and are co-affected in many craniofacial-limb syndromes.

theme: Negative regulation of TLR/IL-1 inflammatory cytokine signalling
story: The centre is restraint of innate inflammatory signalling: dampening of TLR4 (LPS), TLR2 and Toll-family receptor and IL-1 receptor signalling. The cytokine-production terms (reduced IL-1alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-12 and TNF-family production) are the outputs that this restraint limits. As a whole the cluster describes the negative feedback that keeps TLR/IL-1R-driven inflammation in check.

theme: Leukotriene and lipoxygenase-derived eicosanoid metabolism
story: The core is the lipoxygenase branch of arachidonic acid metabolism: synthesis of 5- and 15-HETE derivatives, leukotrienes (LTB4, LTC4, LTD4), eoxins and lipoxins. Leukotriene transport and cysteinyl-leukotriene receptor signalling (driving IL-4) describe their action, while omega-oxidation, icosanoid and leukotriene catabolism describe their inactivation, largely in the ER. The cluster as a whole is about producing, signalling with and clearing pro-inflammatory and pro-resolving lipoxygenase mediators.

theme: Plasma membrane amino acid transporters and their diseases
story: The centre is solute-carrier-mediated amino acid uptake across the plasma membrane, covering neutral amino acids (SLC6A19, proton-coupled transporters), proline, glycine, tryptophan and acidic amino acids (SLC1A1). The disease terms (Hartnup disorder, dicarboxylic aminoaciduria/schizophrenia, obesity-associated SLC6A14) show the clinical consequences of losing specific transporters in kidney, gut and brain. Together the cluster describes amino acid transport and its inherited defects.

theme: Base excision repair, alkylation reversal and active DNA demethylation
story: The centre is base excision repair: DNA glycosylases (OGG1, MUTYH, NTHL1, NEIL1/3) recognise and excise damaged purines and pyrimidines, APEX1 displaces them, and single-nucleotide replacement resolves the abasic site, with many terms describing disease-associated glycosylase defects. Direct reversal of alkylation by MGMT and ALKBH2/3, single-strand break repair and NEIL3-mediated interstrand crosslink repair extend the same damage-repair toolkit. TET/TDG-driven 5-methylcytosine demethylation is included because it reuses BER to remove oxidised methylcytosines, linking repair to epigenetic CpG demethylation.

theme: Lipoylated 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes and branched-chain catabolism
story: The core is the family of mitochondrial 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes (PDH, OGDH, OADH, BCKDH) that share the DLD E3 subunit and require protein lipoylation, together with the glycine cleavage system, which also uses lipoylated proteins. BCKDH and its regulators (BCKDK, PPM1K) and their maple syrup urine disease defects (BCKDHA/B, DBT, DLD) form a prominent disease subcluster, while lysine catabolism via OADH and succinyl-CoA production via OGDH show the metabolic roles. Together the cluster describes the lipoate-dependent oxidative decarboxylation machinery feeding acyl-CoAs into mitochondrial metabolism.

theme: TCA cycle coupled to oxidative ATP synthesis
story: The centre is the tricarboxylic acid cycle and its intermediates (2-oxoglutarate, succinate, malate), with pyruvate supply as an entry point. Succinate dehydrogenase links the cycle directly to the electron transport chain, and proton-motive-force ATP synthesis is the energetic endpoint. Together the cluster depicts mitochondrial oxidative energy metabolism from carbon oxidation to ATP.

theme: Gonadotropin control of ovarian follicle development and ovulation
story: The centre is the ovarian cycle driven by the pituitary: LH and FSH secretion and their feedback regulation, and granulosa/theca responses to these hormones. The ovarian side runs from antral follicle growth and oocyte meiotic maturation through ovulation, luteinization and luteolysis, framed by the estrous cycle and female gonad development. As a whole the cluster describes the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis that produces cyclic ovulation.

theme: RAS-MAPK signalling and its oncogenic and RASopathy mutants
story: The core is RAS GTPase signalling through the MAPK cascade, with GAP-mediated inactivation (including NF1) and positive and negative regulation of Ras signal transduction. The mutant terms (RAS, RAS-GAP, MAP2K and NF1 loss-of-function variants) describe how this pathway is constitutively activated in cancer and RASopathies, while RSK activation and RIT/RIN signalling to p38 represent downstream and parallel branches. Together the cluster depicts the RAS-MAPK pathway and its pathological activation.

theme: Vitamin D activation and renal phosphate homeostasis
story: The centre is mineral homeostasis: vitamin D is hydroxylated to calcitriol by CYP27B1 and inactivated by CYP24A1, and PTH signalling regulates both vitamin D activation and renal phosphate handling. Type II Na+/Pi cotransporters (SLC34A1/2/3) carry out phosphate reabsorption and uptake, and their defects cause hypophosphatemic rickets, nephrolithiasis and pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis, alongside the vitamin D-dependent rickets and hypercalcaemia disorders. Together the cluster describes the endocrine and transport system that keeps calcium and phosphate balanced.

theme: Hepatic glucose-6-phosphate, fructose and glycerol metabolism
story: The centre is the hepatic glucose output machinery: glucose-6-phosphatase and its transporter (G6PC, SLC37A4) at the end of gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis, opposed by glucokinase and its regulatory protein, with corresponding diseases (GSD Ia/Ib, MODY2, G6PC3 neutropenia). Fructose metabolism (fructolysis and its disorders, essential fructosuria and hereditary fructose intolerance) and glycerol/glycerol-3-phosphate and alditol metabolism feed carbons into the same hexose-phosphate and gluconeogenic pool. As a whole the cluster describes how the liver interconverts sugars and glycerol to regulate blood glucose.

theme: Metanephric mesenchyme differentiation and nephron induction
story: The core is development of the permanent kidney from metanephric mesenchyme: mesenchymal cell differentiation, the mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition that forms nephrons, and differentiation of nephron tubule epithelium with proximal/distal patterning. Regulation of metanephros development, kidney size and cell proliferation, and negative regulation of kidney development control the extent of this process, while intermediate mesoderm and pronephros represent its developmental origins. Together the cluster describes how the nephron-forming lineage arises and is regulated.

theme: Nucleotide-sugar supply for glycosylation and GPI anchoring
story: The centre is the supply of activated sugars for glycoconjugate synthesis: the hexosamine pathway (GFPT1, UDP-GlcNAc synthesis), sialic acid/CMP-Neu5Ac metabolism (GNE), UDP-glucose and UDP-glucuronate formation, mannose and dolichol-phosphate-glucose, and SLC35 nucleotide-sugar transporters into the Golgi/ER. These feed N-glycan assembly and processing (ALG14, MOGS, MAN1B1) and GPI anchor synthesis and attachment, while lysosomal oligosaccharide and glucosamine catabolism describe glycan turnover. The many congenital disorders of glycosylation show the clinical consequences of breaks anywhere along this supply chain.

theme: Ciliogenesis and targeting of proteins to the primary cilium
story: The core is building the cilium and delivering cargo to it: basal body anchoring, ciliogenesis, transition-zone localisation, and cargo-targeting routes (BBSome, VxPx/ARF4, ARL13B-INPP5E, myristoylated-protein trafficking). Receptor localisation to the non-motile cilium describes the signalling purpose, while ciliary beat frequency represents motile cilia. Chaperone-mediated complex assembly (BBS chaperonins) and organ identity maintenance are peripheral, reflecting ciliopathy-related components; overall the cluster depicts how cilia are assembled and stocked.

theme: Heme biosynthesis and iron-sulfur cluster assembly
story: The centre is mitochondrial iron cofactor production: heme synthesis through protoporphyrinogen IX to heme B, and assembly of [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] clusters in mitochondria and cytosol. Mitochondrial ABC transporters export the intermediates needed for cytosolic Fe-S assembly and heme handling, and TCA enzyme maturation shows a key consumer of Fe-S clusters. Regulation of tetrapyrrole metabolism and haemoglobin synthesis connect the pathway to erythroid demand; together the cluster describes how cells make their iron-containing prosthetic groups.

theme: MECP2-mediated regulation of neuronal gene expression
story: The centre is MECP2, the methyl-CpG-binding regulator mutated in Rett syndrome: its expression, phosphorylation and binding to 5mC/5hmC DNA, and the loss of these functions. Its target programmes, namely neuronal receptors and channels, GABA signalling genes, neuronal ligands and transcription factors, link it to neuronal excitability terms such as action potential regulation, calcium channel control and metabotropic glutamate signalling. Sensory and visual behaviour terms represent the neurological phenotypes, so the cluster describes MECP2's role in tuning neuronal function.

theme: Nephron segmentation and ureteric bud development in metanephros
story: The core is formation of the nephron in the permanent kidney: metanephric mesenchyme gives renal vesicles, then comma- and S-shaped bodies, which are patterned along the proximal-distal axis into tubules, distal convoluted tubule and loop of Henle. In parallel, the ureteric bud lineage (nephric duct, ureteric bud elongation, collecting duct, ureter) forms the collecting system that induces and connects to nephrons. With intermediate mesoderm and pronephros as origins, the cluster describes kidney organogenesis as a whole.

theme: Motor-driven cargo transport in neuronal axons and dendrites
story: The centre is cytoskeletal transport in neurons: kinesins carry cargo anterogradely along microtubules, moving synaptic vesicles, dense core vesicles and presynaptic proteins to the axon and neurotransmitter receptor complexes into dendrites. Retrograde dense core vesicle transport, actin-based vesicle movement and microtubule depolymerisation (kinesin-13 family) round out the transport machinery. Together the cluster describes how neurons deliver synaptic components to distant compartments.

theme: Glucagon and nutrient signalling controlling gluconeogenesis and lipid storage
story: The centre is the fasting response: glucagon secretion and cellular glucagon signalling activate PKA, which phosphorylates key metabolic factors to drive gluconeogenesis, with positive and negative regulation of gluconeogenesis as the main output. AMPK inhibition of ChREBP, restraint of triglyceride synthesis, and intracellular triglyceride and fatty acid homeostasis describe the coordinated shift away from lipid storage. Response to caloric restriction frames the whole cluster as the hormonal and energy-sensing control of hepatic fuel balance.

theme: Cellular osmoregulation and sodium/potassium/chloride ion transport
story: The centre is cellular water and salt homeostasis: osmosensory signalling and responses to hypo- and hyperosmotic and salt stress, which govern intracellular water balance. The effector side is regulated ion transport, namely sodium transporter activity and export, potassium import, transepithelial chloride transport and renal sodium handling, typified by WNK-SPAK/OSR1-regulated cotransporters and the Na/K pump. Pancreatic juice secretion and potassium responses represent epithelial outputs of the same ion-transport control.

theme: MYC-driven ribosome biogenesis via RNA polymerase I rRNA transcription
story: The core is RNA polymerase I transcription of rRNA genes: preinitiation complex assembly, promoter opening, initiation and escape, plus nucleolar chromatin states set by activators (B-WICH, CSB/G9a) and repressors (NoRC, SIRT1). MYC targets and the MYC transcriptional network describe the growth signal that drives rRNA and Pol III output, while regulation of G1-G0 transition and Pol I repression show the opposite, quiescent state. Together the cluster describes how cells scale ribosome production to growth signalling.

theme: Glutamate/glutamine nitrogen metabolism and dicarboxylate transport
story: The centre is glutamate and glutamine metabolism as the hub of nitrogen handling: glutamine use, glutamate synthesis and catabolism, aspartate/asparagine metabolism, and ammonium homeostasis. The malate-aspartate shuttle and transporters for succinate, tricarboxylates and other organic anions (SLC13, SLC25, SLC17 including the sialin defect in Salla disease) move the carbon skeletons and reducing equivalents that link these amino acids to the TCA cycle. As a whole the cluster describes how cells balance nitrogen disposal and anaplerotic carbon flow.

theme: Protein quality control: ERAD, ubiquitination and selective autophagy
story: The centre is handling of misfolded proteins: recognition and unfolding, ER-associated degradation and its regulation, E3 ubiquitin ligase tagging and Josephin-domain deubiquitinases (ataxin-3). Selective autophagy of organelles, namely reticulophagy and pexophagy, provides the parallel bulk-clearance route, with protein docking, oligomerisation and perinuclear localisation describing aggregate handling. Together the cluster depicts how cells detect and dispose of damaged proteins and organelles.

theme: tRNA charging, modification and translational fidelity
story: The centre is preparation of tRNAs for accurate translation: cytosolic and mitochondrial aminoacylation and tRNA metabolism ensuring fidelity. Modifications at the anticodon (wybutosine at G37, wobble uridine thiolation, wobble guanine modification) and tRNA splicing complete tRNA maturation, while selenocysteine synthesis and translational readthrough represent specialised decoding. Diphthamide synthesis on EEF2 is a related translation-factor modification; together the cluster describes the machinery that ensures codons are read correctly.

theme: Dendritic cell-driven IL-12/IFN-gamma Th1 immunity
story: The centre is the Th1 axis: dendritic cells process and present antigen on MHC I and II, produce IL-12 and other cytokines, and drive naive CD4 T cells to differentiate into Th1 cells. Th1 cells produce IFN-gamma, and the interferon-gamma response and MHC upregulation form a positive feedback loop that further activates antigen-presenting cells. GM-CSF and response to protozoa describe the context, intracellular pathogen defence, so the cluster as a whole depicts type 1 cell-mediated immunity.

theme: Transcriptional repression of cadherin genes in EMT and neural crest
story: The centre is transcriptional control of cadherin genes: positive and negative regulation of CDH1 (E-cadherin), CDH11 and CDH19, the classic switch underlying epithelial-mesenchymal transition and neural crest development. PAX3 target sets and generic transcriptional repression and DNA-binding inhibition terms describe the repressive regulators involved, and TGF-beta/BMP signalling (TGFBR3, BMP module with p15) supplies the upstream inductive cue. Together the cluster depicts the transcriptional programme that changes cell adhesion during developmental and pathological EMT, though the generic repression terms are loose.

theme: Sulfur amino acid and selenium compound catabolism
story: The centre is sulfur amino acid metabolism: transsulfuration and cysteine catabolism produce hydrogen sulfide, which mitochondria oxidise to sulfate, along with alkanesulfonate (taurine-related) metabolism. Selenium compounds (selenomethionine, selenocysteine, methylselenol) are processed by the same enzymes into H2Se and methylated for excretion. Together the cluster describes how cells break down sulfur and its chemical analogue selenium.

theme: Thyroid hormone production and action with sulfonation and selenium
story: The centre is thyroid hormone biology: iodide uptake by NIS (SLC5A5) for hormone generation, thyroid hormone transport, activity regulation and receptor signalling. Selenocysteine synthesis, selenium metabolism and translational readthrough reflect the selenoprotein deiodinases that activate and inactivate thyroid hormones, while PAPS synthesis/transport and cytosolic sulfonation describe sulfation, a route of thyroid hormone inactivation (with PAPSS2 skeletal dysplasia as a related defect). The cluster as a whole describes thyroid hormone synthesis, activation and metabolic clearance.

theme: Detoxification of reactive oxygen species and aldehydes
story: The core is defence against reactive species: ROS detoxification and redox homeostasis. Methylglyoxal and other reactive aldehydes are cleared by glyoxalase and aldehyde-catabolic enzymes, and protein repair reverses the oxidative and glycation damage these agents cause. Together the cluster describes the cell's protection against oxidative and carbonyl stress.

theme: Nutrient and energy sensing by mTORC1
story: The centre is mTORC1 signalling and its positive and negative regulation. Inputs come from amino acids, especially leucine, acting through lysosomal recruitment of mTORC1, from glucose and energy status via LKB1-AMPK, and from lysosomal cholesterol. Rapamycin response reflects pharmacological inhibition; together the cluster describes how mTORC1 integrates nutrient availability to control growth.

theme: p53-mediated DNA damage response: arrest, apoptosis, senescence
story: The centre is p53: its expression, phosphorylation, co-factor association and MDM2/COP1-controlled degradation, plus cancer-associated loss of tetramerisation. Activated by X-ray and gamma-radiation damage, p53 transcribes genes for G1 arrest (p21, CDK inhibition), DNA repair, death receptors and intrinsic apoptosis, and drives replicative senescence. G2 checkpoint signalling, Cdc25A degradation and GTSE1/MASTL recovery describe the coupled cell-cycle checkpoint machinery, so the cluster describes the full DNA damage response deciding between arrest, repair and death.

theme: Glycerolipid synthesis and remodelling: PA, DAG, TAG
story: The centre is the glycerol-phosphate pathway: phosphatidic acid synthesis, conversion to diacylglycerol and then triacylglycerol. Acyl-chain remodelling of DAG and TAG and monoacylglycerol synthesis adjust the fatty acid composition, while hydrolysis of lysophospholipids (LPC, LPE) and glycerophospholipid catabolism return acyl chains and glycerol backbones to this pool. Together the cluster describes the interconversion of glycerolipids for storage and membrane turnover.

theme: Regulation of sprouting angiogenesis and endothelial behaviour
story: The centre is angiogenesis: VEGF receptor signalling drives endothelial activation, proliferation, migration, sprouting, branching and tube morphogenesis. Opposing terms (negative regulation of endothelial proliferation and VEGF production, endothelial apoptosis) represent the brakes, while vascular wound healing, FGF production and fibroblast survival and chemotaxis describe the stromal context of vessel growth. As a whole the cluster describes the positive and negative control of new blood vessel formation.

theme: APOBEC3G cytidine deamination restricting HIV reverse transcription
story: The centre is APOBEC3G-mediated antiviral restriction: this cytidine deaminase is packaged into HIV virions and deaminates cytosines in the viral DNA during minus- and plus-strand synthesis, suppressing replication, while HIV Vif counters it by targeting it for degradation. The HIV early life cycle (binding, entry, uncoating, reverse transcription, frameshifting) provides the stage on which this occurs, and generic C-to-U RNA editing (editosome) and DNA deamination reflect the APOBEC enzyme family. Together the cluster describes host editing enzymes as an intrinsic restriction factor against retroviruses.

theme: Retroviral integration and host control of viral latency
story: The centre is the post-entry retroviral life cycle: nuclear import of the preintegration complex by Vpr, integration of viral DNA into the host genome, and abortive products such as 2-LTR circles and autointegration. Host-mediated activation and suppression of viral transcription determine whether integrated (or herpesviral, HCMV) genomes are expressed or held latent, while APOBEC3G and LRRFIP1-driven type I interferon represent host restriction. As a whole the cluster describes how viral genomes establish themselves in the host and how the host governs their expression.

theme: Innate, social and reward-related animal behaviours
story: The cluster centres on whole-organism behaviour: social and reproductive behaviours (aggression, mating, parental behaviour) with amygdala development as their neural substrate. Reward and learning behaviours (operant conditioning, conditioned place preference, responses to ethanol and nicotine) and basic motor and maintenance behaviours (locomotion, exploration, grooming, drinking, swimming) complete it. It is a broad behavioural-phenotype cluster rather than a single mechanism, unified by mouse behavioural genetics.

theme: Ubiquitin-proteasome system: ubiquitination, deubiquitination and proteasome
story: The centre is the ubiquitin code: E1/E2 activation, E3 ligases, varied chain types (K6, K11, K27, K29, K48, K63, branched), and the opposing deubiquitinase families (USP, UCH, OTU, metalloprotease). The proteasome and its assembly, N-end and C-end degron rules and regulation of proteasomal catabolism describe the degradative endpoint, while TRiC/CCT chaperonin folding and regulation of protein folding represent the folding side of proteostasis. The BTM modules (RB1/BCL2L1, Polycomb with ubiquitin regulation) are loosely attached; overall the cluster describes how ubiquitin tagging controls protein fate.

theme: Platelet activation, adhesion, aggregation and degranulation
story: The centre is platelet activation: adhesion to exposed collagen via GPVI and GPIb-IX-V, and amplification through thrombin PAR, ADP P2Y1/P2Y12 and thromboxane TP receptors. These signals drive degranulation (with SNARE disinhibition), aggregation and coagulation, while prostacyclin signalling and PECAM1 provide inhibitory counterbalance and LDL sensitises platelets. The blood transcriptional modules read out the platelet signature; together the cluster describes haemostatic platelet function.

theme: Cysteinyl-leukotriene and peptide-conjugated lipid mediator metabolism
story: The centre is glutathione-conjugated lipid mediators: leukotriene C4/D4 synthesis via peptide conjugation and modification, with eoxins, and the analogous peptide conjugates of maresins, protectins and resolvins in tissue regeneration. Leukotriene transport and CysLT receptor signalling describe their action, while omega-oxidation and leukotriene, icosanoid and lipoxin catabolism describe inactivation. As a whole the cluster describes production and clearance of conjugated lipid mediators of inflammation and resolution.

theme: TCR signalling and T/NK cell activation signatures
story: The core is T cell receptor proximal signalling: CD3/zeta phosphorylation, ZAP-70 recruitment to the synapse and ITK/PKC-driven differentiation. The blood transcriptional modules for T cell activation and T/NK enrichment and the IL2/IL7/TCR network read out lymphocyte activation, while CD8 alpha-beta and gamma-delta differentiation describe developmental outcomes. Together the cluster depicts antigen-receptor-driven T cell activation.

theme: Th2 type 2 immunity: IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-33
story: The centre is Th2 differentiation and its cytokines: IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13 production and their positive and negative regulation. IL-33 signalling acts as an upstream alarmin, IL-4/IL-13 receptor signalling as the effector pathway, and mast cell activation and humoral antimicrobial responses as downstream effects. Response to nematodes names the physiological purpose, so the cluster describes type 2 immunity against helminths and in allergy.

theme: Myeloid progenitor differentiation into granulocytes and mast cells
story: The centre is transcriptional control of granulopoiesis: PU.1, C/EBP and retinoic acid receptor programmes commit myeloid progenitors to neutrophil, eosinophil and mast cell fates, with the promyelocyte granule-protein module marking an intermediate stage. GM-CSF and CSF receptor signalling drive expansion, and negative regulation of erythrocyte differentiation reflects the myeloid-erythroid fate choice. Together the cluster describes how bone marrow progenitors become granulocytes.

theme: Axial mesoderm, notochord and neural tube patterning
story: The centre is midline patterning of the early embryo: axial mesoderm forms the notochord, which signals (Sonic hedgehog) to induce the floor plate and ventral midline of the neural tube. Neural fold formation, neural plate regionalisation, neuron fate determination and radial glia/neuroepithelial differentiation describe the neural responses, while paraxial mesoderm and body morphogenesis describe the wider axis. Ciliary protein localisation is included because Hedgehog signalling depends on primary cilia; together the cluster depicts establishment of the dorsoventral body axis and neural tube.
